goal.problem: Existing scribe data lives in monolithic JSONL files (notes.jsonl, notes_archive.jsonl, learnings.jsonl) but notes.py now expects the new folder-per-type layout from Phases 1-2.
goal.solution: Write a one-way migration script that converts all existing JSONL records into the new folder-per-type layout with individual .md files and per-folder indexes.
goal.value: Users can transition to the new scribe v2 storage without losing any existing notes, learnings, or history.

components.name: migrate_scribe_v2.py
components.description: Main migration script at scripts/migrate_scribe_v2.py. Reads old JSONL files, creates folder-per-type layout, writes index entries and .md files. Supports --dry-run and --force flags.

components.name: JSONL reader
components.description: Reads notes.jsonl, notes_archive.jsonl, and learnings.jsonl with graceful handling of malformed lines (skip + warn).

components.name: Record converter
components.description: Maps old record fields to new index entry format. Generates summary from content (first 200 chars for long notes). Sets has_body=true for all records.

components.name: Backup of old files
components.description: Before migrating, copies old JSONL files to a backup/ subfolder with timestamp prefix. These are kept for manual rollback.

shape.integration_point: scripts/migrate_scribe_v2.py — standalone script, uses ScribeStore from scribe/store.py for writes.
shape.data_flow: Old JSONL files -> read + parse -> convert records -> ScribeStore.add_note() for each -> verify counts match.
shape.dependencies: scribe/store.py (Phase 1), notes.py rewrite complete (Phase 2) so the new layout is the active one.

behavior.processing: 1. Locate old JSONL files (notes.jsonl, notes_archive.jsonl, learnings.jsonl) in the legacy state dir. 2. If --dry-run, report what would be migrated and exit. 3. Back up old files to backup/ with timestamp. 4. Read each JSONL file line by line, parse records, skip malformed. 5. For each note record: determine type folder, write .md file, write index entry using ScribeStore. Archived notes go to archive/ subfolder. 6. For each learning: write to learnings/ folder. 7. Set next_id to max observed ID + 1. 8. Print summary: N notes migrated, M learnings migrated, K skipped.
behavior.output: Stdout: migration progress and summary. Exit 0 on success, exit 1 on error.

error_cases.behavior: Print 'No legacy data found at <path>', exit 0.

error_cases.trigger: New layout already has data and --force not set
error_cases.behavior: Print warning, refuse to overwrite, exit 1.
Skip with warning, continue migration. Report count of skipped at end.

edge_cases.condition: Note with no 'type' field in old record
Duplicate IDs across notes.jsonl and notes_archive.jsonl
edge_cases.behavior: Archive copy takes precedence (it's the older state). Active copy gets next available ID.
Map learning fields (id with L-prefix, content, timestamp) to learnings/ folder.

in_scope: One-way migration from JSONL to folder-per-type
Backup of old files before migration
Migration of notes, archived notes, and learnings
out_of_scope: Reverse migration (v2 back to JSONL) — not needed
Deletion of old JSONL files — user confirms manually later
Migration of memory/ — already file-per-entry, untouched
must_not_break: Old JSONL files are never modified, only read
If migration fails partway, old data is still intact in backup

acceptance_criteria: Given old notes.jsonl with 50 notes of mixed types, when migrate_scribe_v2.py is run, then each note appears as an .md file in the correct type folder with a matching index entry
Given old notes_archive.jsonl with archived notes, when migration runs, then archived notes appear in <type>/archive/ subfolders
Given old learnings.jsonl with 10 learnings, when migration runs, then all appear in learnings/ with L-prefixed .md filenames
Given --dry-run flag, when migration runs, then no files are created and a summary of what would be migrated is printed
Given the new layout already has data and --force is not set, when migration runs, then it refuses with a clear error
Given a malformed line in notes.jsonl, when migration runs, then that line is skipped with a warning and all other records migrate successfully
Given migration completes, when notes.py list is run, then output matches the pre-migration content
Given migration completes, then old JSONL files exist in backup/ with timestamp prefix
